newsitem.title: USA: Chevron plugs leaking Texas gas line.
newsitem.headline: Chevron plugs leaking Texas gas line.

text.p: Chevron Corp crews overnight plugged a leaking liquified petroleum gas pipeline that forced the evacuation of nearly 4,000 inmates from a state prison near Dayton, Texas, officials said Wednesday.

The prisoners, evacuated Monday to escape the fumes, will begin returning to their cells Thursday after officials check for pockets of the highly flammable gas that may have collected in parts of the sprawling prison complex.

"If everything goes according to plan, we should have those buildings clear by noon Thursday," prison spokesman David Nunnelee said. "It will take another 12 hours to get everyone moved back in and locked down."

The prisoners were evacuated after a billowing cloud of gas began gushing from a section of the pipeline in a field about half a mile from the prison complex, which houses about 3,800 inmates, 2,500 of them women.

Hundreds of inmates have been transferred to nearby prisons, and about 3,500 were being moved to high school gymnasiums in Dayton, about 30 miles northeast of Houston, where they will spend the night, he said.

A short section of the pipeline was plugged overnight and crews injected nitrogen to purge any remaining gas. The line had been carrying 100,000 barrels per day of gas to a plant in Mont Belvieu, Texas east of Houston, where it is processed to make propane, ethane and butane.
"The line will be back intact by mid-afternoon," Chevron spokesman Jerry Barlow said.

The Texas Department Criminal Justice plans to seek reimbursement from Chevron for costs of moving the inmates, including 26 pregnant inmates housed in a medical facility for observation since the line broke, officials said.
